text:
mia: FYI customer (FinRegCo) just made routing guarantees a gating item for Dedicated: per-tenant geo-containment + an opt-out clause for a small set of workloads. We need a short playbook + acceptance checklist we can attach to the quote.

alex: Clarify scope: when they say 'geo-containment' do they mean strict hardware tenancy (dedicated nodes), regional-only routing (never leave eu-west-1), or logical guarantees (encrypted-at-rest + audit logs)? Each has different cost/ops.

sam: From ops: quickest delivery = region-locked routing + tenant slices (logical isolation). True hardware separation requires Dedicated pool capacity planning and lead time for GPUs.

rachel: From SRE: acceptance must include both safety and recovery gates. Suggest: safety = zero cross-tenant data paths in tests, recovery = failover completes within 45s in chaos sim, stability = 7-day p99 latency within X% of baseline.

sophie: Compliance ask: need a signed data residency attestation and a list of all enforcement points (ingest, model cache, logs, backups). Also request proof of KMS separation or tenant-scoped key wrappers.

jenna: Legal: opt-out clause needs exact language: is it "no cross-region routing for specific tenant workloads" or "preferred region only, with emergency evacs allowed". Either way we require a timeboxed pilot exemption + a signed risk appendix if they permanently opt out of fallbacks.

marco: Sales: FinRegCo is willing to pay uplift but wants fixed milestones and rollback protections in contract. They're targeting a pilot in 8 weeks; procurement may add 2-3 weeks if Dedicated hardware is required.

mia: Let's draft a minimal gate matrix that covers PoC -> Canary -> Staged -> GA and include who signs each gate. I'll throw a first cut: 

POC: verify tenant routing tags, isolated prefix routing, KV cache separation; owner=eng-runtime; acceptance=test-suite pass + no cache leakage observed
CANARY: 5 tenants in target region, automated chaos sim for node/region outage, owner=eng-platform+eng-sre; acceptance=<1 incident in 72h + failover_time <45s
STAGED: 25 tenants, perf regression tests, legal artifact checklist complete, owner=product+security; acceptance=<2 SLA violations in 7d + signed attestation
GA: full production roll, finance billing model agreed, owner=all stakeholders; acceptance=contract signoff + audit artifacts

alex: For POC add specific tests: prefix-blacklist test, KV eviction across boundaries, tokenized-input nonce to ensure no leakage. We'll need a deterministically reproducible test harness.

sam: Capacity note: for failover headroom model 1.8-2.0x baseline for burst. Ops will need a dedicated failover reserve bucket or autoscale burst policy for Dedicated. We'll publish the cost model for the uplift.

rachel: Monitoring: add tenant-scoped drift detection and cross-routing alerts. Metrics to capture: failover_time, routed_region, error_rate_by_tenant, cache_hit_ratio_by_tenant. We'll produce Grafana dashboards and an alert runbook.

sophie: Also list audit artifacts: data flow diagrams, KMS key policies, log retention policy, access control matrix, and penetration test summary.

jenna: Billing: customer asked for a separate line item for 'failover compute' — propose we measure 'failover_compute_seconds' (sum of extra vGPU-seconds used when traffic is routed out-of-region) or a simpler per-hour reserved bucket during failover windows. Finance needs acceptance criteria for how that metric is computed.

marco: I'll ask the customer which billing model they prefer. If they want deterministic billing, we should support a dedicated reserved block.

mia: Action owners and rough ETAs: alex (arch doc: routing policy + tag schema + fallback decision tree) in 4 business days; sam (capacity model + runbook + procurement ask) in 3 days; rachel (SLO matrix, chaos scenarios, dashboards) in 2 days; jenna (contract/risk appendix + artifact checklist) in 3 days; sophie (compliance artifacts list and attestation template) in 3 days; marco (customer timeline confirmation) today.

alex: I'll include TTL semantics for tenant tags and a feature-flag design so exemptions can be timeboxed. Technical tradeoff: permanent exemptions require long-lived policy forks and extra ops overhead.

sam: Ops question: who owns emergency evacuations if customer forbids fallback? That needs explicit C-level acceptance; we need a signed waiver template.

jenna: We'll draft a Risk Acceptance Appendix (RAA) with explicit triggers for revocation and indemnity language. No permanent waiver without exec sign-off.

rachel: For launch gates: require a safety gate (no data leakage), a resilience gate (chaos tests pass), and a stability gate (7d SLOs). All three must be green before GA.

mia: Proposed immediate next step: 48-hour working review to align on gate definitions and attachables for the quote. I'll set a review meeting and try to include a customer rep. Can everyone join?

alex: yes

sam: yes

rachel: yes

jenna: yes

sophie: yes

marco: yes, will invite customer contacts

ops-bot: Meeting scheduled: "Tenant geo-containment gating review" on Fri 11:00am PT. Agenda: review PoC/CANARY/STAGED/GA gates, acceptance artifacts, billing model, runbook owners.

mia: Short action list: alex: arch draft (4d); sam: capacity + runbook (3d); rachel: SLO + chaos (2d); jenna: legal RAA + artifacts (3d); sophie: compliance attestation template (3d); marco: customer timeline confirmation (today).

mia: If PoC verification completes in ~3 weeks we can aim for a staged pilot in ~8-10 weeks but emphasize procurement calendar.

alex: I'll enumerate enforcement touchpoints (ingest, model shard placement, KV cache, logs, backups) in the doc.

sam: Ops will add ACL controls for logs and support tenant-scoped diagnostic access only.

rachel: I'll add tenant-scoped alerting and an automated rollback trigger if cross-routing is detected.

mia: Great. I'll assemble a short acceptance checklist from these items and share before the review. Any final thoughts?

marco: Make sure the acceptance doc is attachable to the sales quote and explicitly referenced in the SOW. Customers love clarity.

jenna: Agreed. I'll produce clause snippets to paste into the SOW and RAA.

ops-bot: Reminder: review packet due in 48 hours."
